thread:
emily-cs: FYI customer ACME (ticket #4592) reporting p99 latency jump from ~800ms -> 6s since 03:00 UTC. They see many requests in 'admit_queue' and timeouts. They attached a HAR and a few logs.

maria-support: Thanks — can you post the support link? Any tenant id/route?

emily-cs: https://support.redwood.ai/t/4592 (ACME). Tenant: acme-prod, route: /v1/generate. Sample request id: rQ9k-2026-03-17-01. Customer says issue started after a deploy at ~02:55.

tom-sre: I'll check ingress queue metrics and worker backlog. Pulling admit_queue length now.

tom-sre: Metrics: admit_queue_depth for acme-prod spiked from ~10 -> 450 around 02:58. p95 token latency across pool up to 1.2s, p99 at 5.8s. Error rate (503) up from 0.1% -> 2.3%.

alex-platform: Any recent config changes to admission control or concurrency caps?

jordan-engineer: There was a change in the runtime: adaptive batcher now holds up to 2048ms for bigger batches to improve throughput (PR #4123). Could be increasing head-of-line latency for low-qps tenants.

maria-support: Customer provided a small repro curl that reproduces high tail: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"short"}' -v` — they see long TTFB.

tom-sre: Quick mitigation: for acme-prod bumped tenant concurrency from 8 -> 32 and lowered admission max-hold to 300ms for their routes. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T02:55:12Z - service/runtime v1.18.4 rolled to canary (sha: d4f3a7)

jordan-engineer: Confirmed: the canary included the adaptive-batcher hold increase. Reverting hold increase for canary now.

alex-platform: Also applied tenant rate isolation: moved acme-prod to a separate worker pool temporarily to avoid noisy-neighbor batching.

emily-cs: Sent customer note: "We're investigating and have applied a temporary isolation and concurrency bump. Expect improvement in minutes; will follow up with root cause."

maria-support: Customer reports improvement at 03:10 UTC — p99 down to ~900ms. They're asking for postmortem and whether we can prevent regressions.

tom-sre: Next steps: 1) Roll back adaptive-batcher hold change from canary (in progress). 2) Add a canary perf test that simulates many small concurrent requests to detect HL latency degens. 3) Add tenant-level admission default cap so low-qps tenants aren't starved by large batchers.

jordan-engineer: Patch PR #4187 created to reduce hold from 2048ms -> 200ms for canary and to add feature-flag gating. Running unit + perf.

alex-platform: For immediate safety, proposing: auto-detect long head-of-line for small payloads and prefer fast-path (no batching) if latency sensitive. Filing design doc.

maria-support: Customer wants root cause timeline and ETA for config guard. I'll keep them updated.

emily-cs: Thanks all. Please add any logs or commands here for handoff to SRE postmortem.

tom-sre: Saved relevant graphs to /dashboards/ingress/admit-depth?date=2026-03-17 and exported admit_queue samples. I'll start a postmortem stub in #postmortems.

jordan-engineer: Quick repro for devs: run `stress-client --concurrency 50 --rate 200 --payload small` against canary runtime to reproduce HL. Script posted to repo at tools/bench/hl_repro.sh

maria-support: Marking thread as ongoing, will update when postmortem is linked. :white_check_mark:
